newsitem.title: CHILE: Storm kills at least 10, destroys roads in Chile.
newsitem.headline: Storm kills at least 10, destroys roads in Chile.

text.p: A violent four-day storm killed at least 10 people and destroyed roads and bridges in central Chile, dumping up to 10 times more rain than the area usually gets in a whole year, authorities said on Tuesday.
The Interior Ministry's National Office of Emergencies (ONEMI) said 10 people had drowned in heavy seas or in flash floods triggered by the storm.

The downpour swelled rivers and brooks and caused mudslides that cut off roads along 500 miles (800 km) in central Chile, forcing authorities to close ports on the Pacific and crossings on the Argentine border in the Andes mountains.
Chile's main highway, the Pan-American Route, was blocked at 14 points but later cleared and about 350 towns and villages were isolated as water, mud and debris clogged smaller roads.

President Eduardo Frei flew over the affected areas late on Monday and announced in La Serena, 300 miles (475 km) north of Santiago, that he had renewed an emergency aid package granted to the region after another tempest in June.

Public Works Minister Ricardo Lagos said on Tuesday the Pan-American Route had been cleared but that the problems caused by the rain underscored the need to spend billions of dollars to strengthen Chile's road infrastructure.
"We hope to overcome this through a persistent policy of investments that will involve a tremendous effort to make up for investments that were not made in past years," he said.
Some 18,000 houses built since 1990 under a public housing program had suffered ravages from storms and floods, local newspaper reports said.
